      "observations": [
        "All 24 owned paths and all 1,834 lines of the complete historical diff were read in three contiguous slices. This includes the new generated path/type modules, generator allowlists, Cargo dependency entries, EWS extraction refactor, shared header block, bridge, Graph operation, fake server and test changes. Generated bindings are owned functional scope here, not a bulk exclusion. Product/conditional metadata showed no Suite body in this scope.",
        "The bridge replaces NS_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with a spawned async sync operation and immediate start success. Initial requests select message properties for a folder; continued requests parse and reuse the opaque token URI. Present items emit on_message_created, removed items emit deletion, nextLink fetches another page and only deltaLink publishes the new sync-state token. Every callback/request error can stop this static operation path; earlier callbacks are not rolled back. The logging NAME remains 'sync folder hierarchy' despite the message operation role.",
        "The initial implementation supplies message_size=0 and is_flagged=false and defaults absent/malformed read/preview fields. Its TODOs explicitly defer size, flag status and update support. The accepted later phase calculates extended-property size, reads flag data and attempts on_message_updated before creating only for NS_MSG_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. The initial always-create behavior is not claimed to remain current.",
        "Historical header conversion assembles Date from received time, Message-Id, address fields, Subject and Priority. A provided valid date must parse/format successfully or the helper returns None; other missing or malformed optional getters can omit a field. A recipient requires both non-null name and address in that historical converter, with no general address validation. The generated Importance accessor expects an object containing a string property; no claim is made that an unread real-service response has that shape. The accepted mapper uses sent time, shared Mailbox formatting and a raw-header overlay as later phases.",
        "The EWS HeaderBlock implementation moves into protocol_shared and both protocols use the same header-name constants. The accepted shared header-block blob is exactly 6d6ac7a8926369eb95d0e6a97ace3612eccad802, matching its historical introduction. Indexed name/value access returns illegal-value errors outside the vector and AsRaw joins Name: Value CRLF lines plus a final blank line. Moving this implementation does not add general header-value validation, MIME sending, or parser guarantees.",
        "The direct current listener/native consumer was checked: a create callback builds a database header from the block, applies flags/ID and nonempty preview, commits and reports addition; the token callback stores folder state. Success/failure synchronize counts and forward completion, with a failure permitted to include already-added messages. The existing asynchronous completion lesson is reused only for this matched operation/listener contract; immediate bridge return is not download or persistence completion.",
        "The changed xpcshell test and shared setup were read in full. EWS retains change/deletion/read/flag/real-folder/recipient scenarios. Only testMessageBatchingGraph is newly enabled for Graph; it generates 10 messages, limits a mock page to 4, waits for listener completion and directly asserts created count, no deletes, Message-Id values, Subject values and a nonempty token. It does not assert Graph update/recipient persistence, size/flags/preview correctness or an actual service. Later accepted task registration enables more Graph cases; those later assertions are not credited to this patch.",
        "The initial mock slices folder changes and supports create/delete payloads plus next/delta links, but it explicitly ignores updates. Its final-link branch tests currentChanges rather than its length; an empty array still takes the branch that reads currentChanges.at(-1). The initial batching test does not request an empty incremental continuation. The accepted mock delegates token slicing to getChanges/nextOffset; that helper's internals were not audited here, so no new current empty-page guarantee is inferred.",
        "Manual test/assertion review: the direct new batching assertions all have nonempty expected-behavior messages containing 'should'. The refactored EWS update helper also retains an older assertion comparing deleted-ID count with the number of updated-message IDs; that count does not verify updated identities. Scalar deepEqual calls are local existing choices, not a general recommendation. Shared test-head setup owns shutdown/server cleanup; the test's removed inline stop cleanup is replaced by those actual helpers.",
        "Manual naming/comments/style review: ewsClient/graphClient and separate incoming-server names expose protocol ownership. The Rust output-producing map/filter_map pipelines build recipient strings, while explicit loops perform sync callbacks. The accepted scoped xpcshell configuration/head exception and Rust lint wrapper were checked; no lint or formatter ran. Reviewers disagree about literal header strings versus constants; the author keeps constants. The optional if-let conversion and doc-summary blank line are actually landed, but neither preference dispute nor memory-churn speculation creates a global rule or benchmark.",

Historical failed lint/build events, later completed builds, Try links, a requested rebase and the author's same-batch send-change explanation remain reports, not fresh execution. Related follow-ups 2025009, 2025016 and 2025019 and the external OpenAPI metadata/documentation bodies were not read.",
